ECE 6390 / Antennas and arrays

Circular aperture

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows how a circular aperture produces a central maximum and surrounding diffraction rings.

A uniformly illuminated disk sums contributions over two dimensions. Its scalar disk field factor is Fₙ = 2J₁(u)/u, with u = π(D/λ)sin θ. The limit at u = 0 is 1.

Power is |Fₙ|². A negative field factor represents a phase reversal, while intensity remains nonnegative. The first positive zero of J₁ is approximately 3.831706, giving sin θnull ≈ 1.2197λ/D.

The class scalar option includes an additional cos θ obliquity factor. State which model is used when comparing half-power widths; HPBW is the full angle between the two half-power crossings.

Example

For D = 10λ, the disk-factor first null is approximately 7.0° from boresight. This one-sided null angle differs from full half-power beamwidth.

    Practice

    1. Why should the expression 2J₁(u)/u be assigned the value 1 at boresight rather than treated as an infinite or missing field?

    Use the small-u behavior J₁(u) ≈ u/2.

    The numerator and denominator vanish together, and their ratio tends to 1. The apparent singularity is removable.
